NDT training in Washington DC: how it works for Washington DC employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for employers and technicians across Washington DC and the surrounding Maryland and Virginia region. We have no classroom in the District. Theory runs live online or in scheduled cohorts, and practical training runs onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you under its written practice.

Washington DC's NDT market is shaped by federal ownership. The District itself has little heavy industry, but it owns, funds or regulates a very large amount of inspected infrastructure. That includes the Washington Navy Yard, headquarters of Naval Sea Systems Command, the Metrorail system, Potomac and Anacostia bridges, federal buildings under constant renovation, and utility and wastewater plants. Around the District sit naval research and test centres, air bases, nuclear and gas-fired power stations, an LNG terminal on the Chesapeake, interstate pipelines and one of the largest data-centre construction markets in the world in Northern Virginia. The NDT work across that region is mostly structural, defence, aerospace and power-related, and the specifications change from contract to contract.

The region adds one complication most cities don't have: three regulatory jurisdictions within a short drive. The District is not an NRC Agreement State. Maryland and Virginia are. A radiography crew working in Northeast DC in the morning and Prince George's County in the afternoon has crossed a regulatory boundary. The same applies to training choices. A technician working for a defence contractor may need NAVSEA-compliant qualification, while one on a bridge contract works to AWS D1.5 and state DOT requirements. SNT-TC-1A training is the common foundation. What sits on top of it depends on the contract.

To plan a programme, request a Washington DC training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Washington DC

Every course follows SNT-TC-1A topical outlines and produces documented classroom hours for your written practice. The table shows typical uses in the DC region. It describes local demand patterns rather than any specific employer's requirements.

MethodLevelsWhat Washington DC employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, III prepBridge and building steel weld examination, transit structure inspection, thickness surveys on utility and plant pipingNone for Level I; Level II requires Level I plus documented experience
PAUT (phased array)II, III prepComplete-joint-penetration welds on structural and bridge steel, naval and defence fabrication welds, power pipingUsually UT Level II per the written practice
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, III prepThick-section welds in power-generation and heavy fabrication, crack sizingUsually UT Level II
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepPiping and pressure-system welds, naval and defence components, castingsNone for Level I; NRC or state radiation-safety requirements apply separately to source users
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, III prepStructural steel and bridge welds, transit and rail components, defence hardwareNone for Level I
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, III prepAerospace and defence components, stainless and non-ferrous welds, research-facility hardwareNone for Level I
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepStructural weld inspection on buildings, bridges and data centres, condition surveys on federal facilitiesNone for Level I
ET (eddy current)I, II, III prepAircraft inspection at military air stations, condenser and heat-exchanger tubes at power plantsNone for Level I

VT, MT and UT are the everyday methods of the DC construction and infrastructure market. Federal and commercial buildings, data centres in Loudoun and Prince William counties, highway interchanges and bridge rehabilitation projects all generate structural weld inspection to AWS D1.1 and, for bridges, AWS D1.5. Level I UT covers theory, straight-beam work and calibration. Level II adds angle-beam weld examination and evaluation against acceptance criteria.

PAUT and TOFD suit UT Level II technicians moving into structural, power and defence fabrication work where encoded ultrasonic records are increasingly specified. Both courses cover scan planning, focal laws, encoded data collection and analysis.

RT is used on piping, pressure systems, castings and defence hardware. The course covers exposure technique, film and digital imaging, image quality indicators and interpretation. Radiation-safety licensing is separate and, in this region, depends on which side of the District line you are working on.

PT and ET matter for the region's aerospace and defence work, including naval air test and evaluation in southern Maryland and airlift operations at Joint Base Andrews, as well as for power-station tube inspection. Defence and aerospace employers may qualify personnel to NAS 410 or NAVSEA requirements rather than SNT-TC-1A alone. Some local employers ask for those, and Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based, so confirm with your Level III how the hours will be credited.

Level III candidates can use our ASNT Level III exam preparation. All courses are listed on the NDT training programmes page.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Washington DC, step by step

SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based. In the DC region, the employer might be a structural steel fabricator, an inspection firm on a transit or bridge contract, a defence contractor or a utility.

  1. Start with the employer's written practice. It defines methods and levels, training and experience minimums, exam rules, the responsible Level III and recertification. On federal and defence contracts, the contracting officer or prime contractor may also require the written practice to meet additional specifications, so read the contract before building the programme.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Atlantis delivers this online, in cohorts or onsite. Required hours come from the written practice, normally following SNT-TC-1A's recommended minimums. See the training requirements matrix.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. Documented hours in the method, at the level sought, verified by a supervisor. Security-controlled sites can make access hard, so keep your logs thorough and current.
  4. Pass general, specific and practical examinations. General covers method theory. Specific covers your employer's procedures, equipment and the codes it works to, whether AWS D1.1 and D1.5, ASME Section V and B31.1, or defence specifications. Practical is performed on real specimens and graded by or under a Level III.
  5. Pass the vision examination. Near-vision and colour contrast, repeated as required.
  6. Receive employer certification. Signed by the employer's certifying authority on the Level III's recommendation.
  7. Recertify on schedule. Within the interval in the written practice. Federal contracts often ask for certification records at bid or mobilisation, so expired paperwork can cost work.

Our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide explains each step in more depth, including crediting prior military NDI experience.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Washington DC crews

Atlantis has no physical training centre in Washington DC. In a region where getting across the Beltway can take longer than a training module, flexible delivery is useful anyway. We offer three routes.

  • Live online theory. Real-time instructor-led classes for the classroom portion. This avoids the commute and suits technicians working night shifts on transit or bridge projects, where much work happens during overnight track and lane closures. See NDT training online.
  • Classroom cohorts. For groups needing the same method and level, at an arranged venue.
  • Onsite at your facility. At your shop, yard or plant, using your equipment, procedures and representative specimens. For employers on secure sites, onsite delivery can be arranged at a location outside the controlled area, such as your own shop, with site access and escort requirements agreed in advance.

Scheduling in the DC region follows several calendars. Power-station outages are typically planned for spring and autumn, outside the summer and winter demand peaks. Transit and bridge work is scheduled around lane and track closures, often at night and at weekends. Construction inspection peaks with project milestones. Defence work follows contract schedules. We usually run theory online during busy periods and schedule onsite practical sessions and examinations for agreed windows.

Ask about onsite training for your Washington DC crew. For multi-site employers, see our corporate NDT training programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Washington DC

Naval and defence. The Washington Navy Yard is home to Naval Sea Systems Command, which sets NDT requirements for naval shipbuilding and repair through its own technical publications. The region also has Naval Surface Warfare Center Carderock in Maryland, Naval Air Station Patuxent River in southern Maryland, the naval surface warfare centres at Dahlgren and Indian Head, and Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling and Joint Base Andrews. Contractors supporting these organisations may be required to qualify NDT personnel to NAVSEA or other military specifications, with SNT-TC-1A as a foundation or alongside it. Military NDI veterans form a large part of the regional NDT workforce.

Transit and rail. The Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority runs Metrorail and Metrobus across the District, Maryland and Virginia. Elevated structures, bridges, track components and rolling-stock maintenance generate VT, MT, UT and ET work. Commuter and freight rail add more.

Bridges and highways. The District Department of Transportation, Maryland and Virginia DOTs, and the National Park Service, which owns several Potomac crossings including Arlington Memorial Bridge, manage bridges that need ongoing inspection and rehabilitation. The Federal Highway Administration's Turner-Fairbank Highway Research Center in McLean, Virginia, runs NDE research for highway infrastructure. Bridge steel work follows AWS D1.5.

Construction and data centres. Federal building renovations, commercial construction in the District and the data-centre boom in Northern Virginia generate large volumes of structural steel inspection to AWS D1.1, plus inspection of generator fuel systems, cooling plant and piping.

Power and energy. The Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant in Maryland and North Anna in Virginia run outage NDT under nuclear-industry qualification programmes, which add requirements beyond basic SNT-TC-1A. Gas-fired and other generating stations across Maryland and Virginia use power piping built to ASME B31.1, with UT, RT, ET and MT during outages. The Cove Point LNG terminal on the Chesapeake Bay and interstate pipelines crossing the region add API 1104 pipeline and plant-integrity work. The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration, which regulates US pipeline safety, is headquartered in the District.

Radiography licensing in DC, Maryland and Virginia. This matters more here than almost anywhere else. Washington DC is not an NRC Agreement State, so the NRC, through its Region I office, licenses radioactive materials such as industrial radiography sources used in the District. DC Health oversees x-ray equipment and certain other radiation sources. Maryland (Department of the Environment) and Virginia (Department of Health) are Agreement States with their own licensing. A radiography company working across all three needs the correct licence or reciprocity in each. Federal facilities can involve further exclusive-jurisdiction rules. Individual radiographers must meet radiation-safety training and certification requirements such as those in the NRC's industrial radiography rules at 10 CFR Part 34. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is a separate NDT credential.

Level III services and written practices for Washington DC NDT companies

DC-region NDT companies often grow on federal and infrastructure contracts, and those contracts ask for documentation early. A proposal or pre-award audit may need the written practice, current certification records, procedures and the Level III's qualifications. Small firms without a full-time Level III, and firms that have added PAUT or moved into defence work without updating their written practice, are most at risk.

  • Written practice development. We draft or revise your written practice against the current SNT-TC-1A edition and structure it so contract-specific requirements can be added cleanly. See written practice development.
  • Outside Level III services. Examination administration, procedure and technique review, and certification-record management.
  • Bid and audit readiness. Review of certification files, training records, experience logs and vision tests ahead of proposals, pre-award audits and client audits.

Book a Level III consultation for your Washington DC company, and see our SNT-TC-1A guidance.

Practise before the practical exam

The practical exam decides most certification attempts. The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. DC-region candidates heading into structural work will find the welding workshop most useful, and those going into military or aerospace work, the hangar.

The simulator is practice only. It does not replace hands-on practical training or the practical exam on real specimens under a Level III. For written exams, work through our UT Level 2 practice questions and related sets.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop writes course content to SNT-TC-1A topical outlines and oversees practical sessions and examinations as the responsible Level III. DC-region employers arranging onsite programmes plan them directly with him.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Washington DC

How do I get NDT certified in Washington DC?

Choose a method that DC-region employers use, with VT, MT and UT for structural and infrastructure work. Complete formal Level I training, build logged experience and pass your employer's general, specific and practical exams plus a vision test. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice.

Can I take NDT training online in the DC area?

Yes, for the classroom portion, through live online classes. Practical training and exams must be hands-on and are delivered onsite at your employer's facility. See NDT training online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the classroom and experience hours in your employer's written practice, usually based on SNT-TC-1A recommendations. Classroom time is short compared with building documented experience. See the training requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Washington DC?

The company needs the right licence. In the District, radioactive materials are licensed by the NRC because DC is not an Agreement State, and DC Health covers x-ray equipment. Maryland and Virginia license through their own state programmes. Individual radiographers must meet radiation-safety training and certification requirements. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is separate.

What does NDT training cost in Washington DC?

We do not publish prices. Cost depends on method, level, group size and delivery format. Request a Washington DC training quote and you will receive a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by DC-area employers?

SNT-TC-1A is widely used by the region's structural, infrastructure, power and industrial employers. Defence and aerospace contracts may add NAVSEA, NAS 410 or other requirements. SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based and is re-issued by each new employer.

Can military NDI experience count toward civilian certification?

Often. Your employer's Level III decides how documented military training and experience are credited under the written practice. Formal SNT-TC-1A training and employer exams usually close the gap. Bring your records to a Level III consultation.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Washington DC?

No. We deliver live online theory, cohorts at arranged venues and onsite training at your facility.

Do you train for NAVSEA-specified NDT work?

Our courses are SNT-TC-1A-based. They cover method fundamentals that underpin defence work, but NAVSEA-specific qualification requirements are set by the contract and your Level III. Check what the contract requires before enrolling.

Do you offer CWI, API or NAS 410 courses?

No. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Those credentials come through their own schemes.

Which method should I start with for DC construction work?

VT and MT are the quickest routes into structural inspection. UT then opens up complete-joint-penetration weld examination on buildings, bridges and data centres.

How do I prepare for ASNT Level III?

Our Level III exam preparation covers the Basic exam and method exams.
